finding_at_baseline.note: The state surveyed at commit 2193ed88, before ADR-0074 (#538) removed the duplicated four-pole verifier. That merge deleted 8 test modules, all from the one optional-ci directory tests/wat/external_verifier/, so the current tree is 413 modules with the unassigned count unchanged at 177. These numbers are kept because the reports quote them; `measured` below is the live count and is re-derived on every run.
finding_at_baseline.deviation_from_the_static_survey: The 2026-09-14 survey at commit 9bb5ab1 reported 418 / 189 / 218-in-any-lane. Four of the five differences are method, one is the tree: (1) three modules run via `python -m unittest`, not pytest — one of them, tests/audit/test_wirelang_spec_freeze_seal_probe.py, in the REQUIRED 'wirelang spec v0.4.3 freeze-seal probe' context, so a pytest-only scan under-reports required coverage by one; (2) tests/live_vm/ is targeted through a bash array (PYTEST_ARGS) that a line scan does not expand; (3) the tree itself gained tests/workflows/test_required_context_error_propagation.py between 9bb5ab1 and this baseline. Direction of the correction: slightly better than reported, and not in a way that changes the conclusion.

measured.method: tooling/ci/lane_inventory.py (static targeting, including the jobs that inherit the acceptance-gate aggregator's enforcement) cross-checked against a real pytest run of every lane target
measured.python: 3.14.7 local; the required lanes pin 3.12 (tests.yml) and 3.13 (runtime-acceptance-gates.yml)
measured.note: Live counts. tests/lanes/test_lane_assignment.py::test_measured_counts_are_current re-derives these from the workflows on every run, so they cannot go stale in a report. After the Welle-3 lane promotion (ADR-0075) `unassigned` is 0: 97 modules went into required lanes, 80 into the non-blocking observation lane with a promotion date of 2026-10-31, and the standing exceptions keep their dates — which are now compared against the calendar by tooling/ci/exemption_expiry.py instead of merely being well-formed.

required_contexts_source: GET /repos/wakir-labs/wakir-runtime/branches/main/protection, read 2026-09-14. Branch protection is not readable from a workflow without a token, so the list is pinned here; test_lane_assignment.py asserts every entry still matches a job display-name in .github/workflows/.
zero_collect_allowed_note: Allow-list for the zero-collection half of the collect gate: a module a lane targets but that yields no node IDs. EMPTY at this baseline, and that is the state to defend. It held two entries until ADR-0074 (#538) removed the duplicated four-pole verifier; both were matrix-only import guards. test_allow_lists_have_no_stale_entries keeps dead entries from accumulating.
import_guard_allowed_note: Names a module-level pytest.importorskip() may legitimately fail on in the production profile. EMPTY at this baseline: every module-level guard in the tree now names something pyproject.toml declares (rfc8785, jsonschema and hypothesis via the `test` extra, PyYAML via `persona`, cryptography) or an in-repo package (wat.*, wirelang.*). An entry here is a wheel the repository installs somewhere without declaring it — write the reason, or declare it.

phase-3c-opt-in.reason: Phase-3c cutover acceptance and rollback drills: 19 modules, 207 tests, every one carrying phase_3c_acceptance / phase_3c_doppel_welle_acceptance / phase_3c_rollback_drill. The markers are documented as opt-in via WAKIR_PHASE_3C_* or the matching --phase-3c-* / --rollback-drill flag. Measured: no workflow in this repository sets any of those variables or passes any of those flags. The opt-in has never been taken, so these 207 tests have never run in CI — the acceptance criteria for a cutover are written down and unexecuted. Skip-by-default is a legitimate design; skip-always is a different thing and needs a decision.

phase-3-skeleton-opt-in.reason: Phase-3 acceptance-gate skeleton behind the phase_3_skeleton marker, opt-in via WAKIR_PHASE_3_SKELETON=1. No workflow sets that variable, so the skeleton has never been exercised. Named as a placeholder rather than a contract in force — which is defensible, and now written down instead of implied.

live-vm-operator.reason: TV-LVD live-VM acceptance. Reachable only through workflow_dispatch in live-vm-acceptance.yml and additionally gated by the --run-live-vm flag plus WAKIR_LIVE_VM_ACCEPTANCE=1. The design reason is sound — it needs a real Proxmox VM and cannot run on a GitHub runner. The evidence is not: the workflow has never been dispatched since it was added on 2026-05-16, so the module has never executed anywhere this repository can observe. 'Runs by operator hand' is at this point an untested claim about the operator.

sbom-baseline-operator.reason: SBOM baseline refresh is an operator-hand action (sbom-baseline-refresh.yml, workflow_dispatch only) because it rewrites a committed baseline; running it automatically would let the baseline chase the artefact instead of pinning it. That reasoning stands. What does not stand is the implied 'and an operator does run it': the workflow has zero runs since it was added.

spec-audit-evidence.reason: Spec/ADR cross-audit and evidence-integrity suites. The group deliberately still mixes two kinds: durable domain invariants (protocol mirror seed integrity, spec cross-validation) and historical state audits (ADR errata cross-audit, final-wave sealing audit). Splitting them is the protocol owner's task before the promotion date — the durable half belongs in a required lane, the historical half belongs on a weekly cadence rather than a per-pull-request one, and promoting the group wholesale would fix the wrong thing in place.
spec-audit-evidence.on_review_date: promote to a required lane, or renew the exception with renewed_on + renewal_reason. An expired date fails the lane-assignment suite in the required production context.

orchestrator-substrate.reason: Hermetic shape tests for compose files, Quadlet units, NATS KV provisioning and the Proxmox bring-up scripts — the remainder after the five trust-bearing modules (the hermetic counterparts of the required digest-pin context) were promoted to a required lane in Welle 3. Same reasoning as infra-substrate: the subject matter touches podman and SSH, so CI behaviour gets measured before it gets a veto.
orchestrator-substrate.on_review_date: promote to a required lane, or renew the exception with renewed_on + renewal_reason. An expired date fails the lane-assignment suite in the required production context.

infra-substrate.reason: Bootstrap, Quadlet, cosign-policy and acceptance-gate consistency tests. 22 of the 29 modules speak to podman, SSH or Proxmox; locally they skip cleanly, on a GitHub runner their behaviour was unmeasured when this group was written. That is the reason they are in the observation lane and not in a required one: making them blocking first and finding out afterwards produces pressure to get tests green rather than pressure to get the system right.
infra-substrate.on_review_date: promote to a required lane, or renew the exception with renewed_on + renewal_reason. An expired date fails the lane-assignment suite in the required production context.

spire-federation-substrate.reason: infra/spire/**/tests/ — a third test root that is neither tests/ nor wirelang/ and was invisible to testpaths and to every lane until the lane inventory made it visible. 14 modules, 196 tests, hermetically green in 5 s locally. Covers the federation bundle rotator, health endpoint status codes and the Prometheus metrics surface. Observation first because this root has never run in CI at all, not once, and a root's first CI run should not also be its first veto.
spire-federation-substrate.on_review_date: promote to a required lane, or renew the exception with renewed_on + renewal_reason. An expired date fails the lane-assignment suite in the required production context.

script-driver.reason: Hermetic tests for operational scripts (backend/routing decision observability, soak probes, the phase-3b live-VM driver, the legacy env-flag migration detector). The scripts are operator-hand; their tests are not, and ran nowhere. Lowest trust-bearing content of the Welle-3 inventory, which is why they are the clearest observation-lane candidates rather than an argument for delay.
script-driver.on_review_date: promote to a required lane, or renew the exception with renewed_on + renewal_reason. An expired date fails the lane-assignment suite in the required production context.

execution_evidence_note: Read 2026-09-14 from GET /repos/wakir-labs/wakir-runtime/actions/workflows/{file}/runs. An exemption that says 'runs by operator hand' or 'opt-in' is a claim about something happening somewhere, and this week produced three counter-examples in three repositories. So every group states the mechanism that would run it, what enables that mechanism, and when it last actually ran. A group whose mechanism nothing enables does not get to be a standing exception: test_standing_exceptions_must_have_actually_run requires a review date for it, exactly like an accident.

lane_promotion.enforcement_note: The three lane-* jobs are not branch-protection contexts. They are dependencies of the `runtime acceptance gates` aggregator, which carries `if: always()` and turns each `needs.<job>.result` into its own exit code before doing anything else — so they block merges exactly as hard as it does. tooling/ci/lane_inventory.py grants that inherited `required` profile only while all three halves of the propagation hold; drop one and the modules fall back to `optional-ci` and this file stops matching the tree.
